chunks: Like ashes are the deeds of those who deny their Lord, which the wind blows away on a windy day. They shall have no power over what they earned. This is the farthest limit of going astray.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the metaphor of ashes in Surah Ibrahim regarding the deeds of disbelievers?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (14:18) is often contrasted with the 'good soil' of the believers in the preceding verse, emphasizing that disbelief renders deeds structurally void rather than merely unrewarded. The metaphor of 'ash' (ramad) signifies total dissolution and lack of cohesion, illustrating that without the foundational faith (Iman) and divine guidance, all accumulated actions are scattered and lost on the Day of Judgment. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the unity of faith and action, where the quality of belief determines the durability of deeds.
